title: Spinach and zucchini frittata
summary: A thick Italian-style omelette, started on the stove and finished in the oven, packed with greens and basil.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a 25 cm (10 in) ovenproof non-stick skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and zucchini 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly coloured.
Add the garlic and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the pan is fairly dry.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and basil. Pour into the pan and stir gently once to spread the vegetables.
Cook over medium-low heat without stirring for 4–5 minutes, until the edge is set.
Move to the oven and bake 10–12 minutes, until the centre is just set. Rest 5 minutes, then loosen and cut into wedges.
tips: Good at room temperature, which is how it is often eaten in Italy.

origin.history: Frittata is the Italian word for a flat egg dish fried in a pan, cooked through rather than folded like a French omelette, and often filled with whatever vegetables are in season. It appears in Italian household cookbooks of the 1800s and was eaten long before.
